Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a list of items we need to evaluate hosting options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). High level constraints:

- CardioSense processes PHI (ECG traces + patient identifiers) so we need a BAA and evidence of HIPAA controls.
- SOC 2 Type II or equivalent evidence for the inference runtime and the control plane.
- Data residency: primary in us-east-1; possible on-prem in a partner datacenter later.
- Key management: customer KMS or HSM required for private deployments.
- Audit window: We have an internal security review scheduled for 2027-06-10 and would like to have evidence before then.

Questions we have today:
1) Which deployment mode do you recommend for a production PHI workload that needs BAA and SOC2 evidence?
2) Can Redwood sign a BAA now, and do you have a draft we can share with legal?
3) What SOC2 artifacts can you provide (report, bridge letter, scope)?
4) For Private (VPC/on-prem) — what is the typical lead time and do you support on-prem installers for isolated datacenters?

I attached our short security questionnaire (two pages) — appreciate if you can respond inline.

Best,
Sam

Hi Sam —

Great to connect — thanks for the clear list. High-level recommendations up front: for PHI in production we usually recommend Dedicated capacity or Private VPC depending on how strict your network isolation and KMS requirements are. Quick decision guide: 

- Hosted API: fastest to launch, can be paired with a signed BAA, but does not support customer-managed on-prem KMS or fully air-gapped on-prem installs. Use if you can accept Redwood-managed keys and the data residency controls in our hosted regions.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): strong isolation at the tenant level, supports BAA + SOC2 (we can scope the runtime). Supports customer VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for many customers — good middle ground.
- Private VPC / On‑prem: required if you need an air-gapped or partner datacenter on-prem package and full control of KMS/HSM. Longer lead time, but matches the strictest compliance needs.

Attached: a draft BAA and a short checklist answering items from your questionnaire. Karthik and Marissa are looped in for technical and contractual follow-ups.

Next steps I propose: 
1) We provide the SOC2 Type II report + bridge letter and the draft BAA (attached) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Karthik will reply with answers to the questionnaire items that are infra-specific (KM, logging, retention).
3) If you prefer Dedicated or Private, let us know target go-live and we will propose a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones.

Proposed quick call: Fri 2027-05-07 09:00 PT to align on scope & MAP — is that OK?

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Nishant / team —

Answers inline to the specific asks: 

- Data controller vs processor: CardioSense would be the controller; Redwood acts as a data processor for inference requests when processing PHI. We can add standard controller/processor language into the BAA.

- Subprocessors: Our main subprocessors for hosted control plane and telemetry are listed here: AWS (us-east-1 for hosted workloads), Datadog (metrics), and S3-compatible storage used for logs (encrypted at rest). For Dedicated deployments we minimize external subprocessors — we can provide a filtered list scoped to the deployment. Full subprocessor list and locations will be attached in the SOC2 package we share.

- SOC2 artifacts & timing: We can provide our SOC2 Type II report (current period through 2027-03-31) and a bridge letter covering changes since the report. Expect delivery of PDF + summary tomorrow EOD. The SOC2 scope includes the Redwood control plane and the inference runtime that we run in our managed Dedicated environment. For Private/on-prem deployments, many infra controls (physical, network) fall in-customer scope — we'll document the split.

- KMS / HSM: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS for Dedicated and VPC options (bring-your-own-KMS). For on-prem HSMs, we support integration patterns (KMIP) but full on-site HSM provisioning is part of our private deployment engineering engagement — typical lead time 8–12 weeks depending on approvals and network readiness.

- Logging & audit: We provide request-level audit logs for inference calls (timestamp, model, tokens, request id) retained according to your policy; retention is configurable. We can stream logs to your SIEM over TLS or provide exports.

- Lead times: Dedicated (reserved capacity) onboarding typical 2–4 weeks after contract + infra prep; Private VPC/on-prem: 6–12 weeks depending on network & security approvals.

Next concrete items from us: SOC2 + bridge + subprocessor list (tomorrow EOD), signed BAA draft for your review, and a proposed MAP doc with milestones for Dedicated vs Private by Monday 2027-05-10.

Happy to discuss on the 09:00 PT call if that still works.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
